title: Trivial square-zero extension of a ring by a module
statement: For a commutative ring $R$ and an $R$-module $M$, the trivial square-zero extension $R\oplus M$ is the $R$-algebra with underlying set $R\times M$, componentwise addition, unit $(1,0)$, and multiplication $(r,m)(s,t)=(rs,rt+sm)$. It is Mathlib's `TrivSqZeroExt R M`, with constants `TrivSqZeroExt.inl` and infinitesimals `TrivSqZeroExt.inr`. The projection to $R$ is `TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom`; an $R$-linear map $M\to N$ induces the algebra map `TrivSqZeroExt.map`. In particular, for a field $K$ and a natural number $n$, `TrivSqZeroExt K (Fin n → K)` is the algebra with basis $1,\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n$ and $\epsilon_i\epsilon_j=0$; `TrivSqZeroExt.map (LinearMap.proj i)` keeps the $i$th infinitesimal coordinate.
